message:
The raw packet data is allocated as a single buffer for the whole packet. The UDP payload is within this buffer, so reading 4 bytes past the UDP payload (at offset 20 within the payload) still falls within the overall packet buffer (since the packet is 59 bytes total). So no heap-buffer-overflow occurs.

The heap-buffer-overflow would only trigger if the UDP payload is at the very end of the allocated buffer. But since the packet buffer contains the Ethernet + IP + UDP headers before the payload, the payload is not at the end.
